notes: Zone v_lots_s: the parking lots of the Village area south of y 1050 (Lot 41, Lot 27, Lot 29, the Children's Center parking strip, Lot 28 with the paved apron in front of the NJ Transit Deck, Lot 47). Frame: model metres, +X east, +Y north. Each lot was read in its own straightened frame (origin and angle in the generator) on rectified NJ 2020 ortho crops at 10 to 50 px/m, with the hillshade and nDSM for edges and poles; names from OSM parking areas (the Children's Center strip has none in OSM: V_lot_CC). Stall rows: dividers found as brightness peaks on transects across each row, then a least-squares fit of the row line, pitch and skew to the line centres sampled at five points along every divider (generated dividers within 0.2 m of the paint along the whole row, except beside parked cars where the detector catches the car edge); rows that change pitch or skew are split into runs. Divider ends from brightness profiles along the dividers. Rows or stalls hidden by cars or shade are inferred from the pitch and say so. Accessible stalls: blue aisles drawn as plain blue areas (the white hatching over them and the wheelchair symbols are not drawn; symbols are plain blue squares). Hatched caps are single lines. Mouths onto Clove Road and Village Road are cut on the road's curb line; the drives, roads and sidewalks are another zone's. Lamps: the 2017 LiDAR shows no isolated pole returns in any of these lots (Lot 27's two pole-mounted heads and the small posts along its east edge are visible only in the 2020 ortho, so they have no height). Lot 29: a painted pedestrian walkway (two rails with slanted bars at 1.83 m) runs along the west side of the aisle; a second one (zigzag at 2.07 m, drawn as bars) along the north part; both are drawn as paint. Lot 28: four rows of 17 stalls, the middle two double rows on painted centre lines, a wedge island at the north, and an east column along the trees that is faint. Lot 47: a loop round a planted island with a walk through it; its south loop lies under the leaning roof of Sinatra Hall in the ortho and follows OSM and the curve.
